He played in the [[NBA]] for the [[Houston Rockets]], [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] and [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. ==Early life== Patterson, born in [[Washington, D.C.]],{{cite web|title=USABasketball Bio: Patrick Patterson|publisher = USA Basketball, Inc.|date=March 21, 2007|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/biosmen/patrick_patterson_bio.html|access-date = May 24, 2007 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070514083638/http://www.usabasketball.com/biosmen/patrick_patterson_bio.html |archive-date = May 14, 2007}} grew up in [[Huntington, West Virginia]]{{cite web |date=May 16, 2007 |title=ESPN Recruit Tracker: Patrick Patterson |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player?id=43944 |access-date=June 5, 2023 |work=ESPN.com}} and graduated from [[Huntington High School (West Virginia)|Huntington High School]] in 2007. During his high school career, Patterson helped lead Huntington High School to three straight state championships. Patterson won his third state championship during his senior season with help from [[O. J. Mayo]]. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Patterson was listed as the No. 3 power forward and the No. 17 player in the nation in 2007,{{Cite web |title=Patrick Patterson Recruiting Profile |url=https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Patrick-Patterson-33871;_ylt=AgkN9EaiyhcurmH4mU3U.87XO5B4 |url-status=dead |access-date=February 6, 2015 |archive-date=February 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150206124821/https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Patrick-Patterson-33871;_ylt=AgkN9EaiyhcurmH4mU3U.87XO5B4 }} and was named a [[McDonald's All-American]]. ==College career== Patrick Patterson played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]] (UK). He chose to play for Kentucky rather than [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] or [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] in a highly publicized recruiting battle. He was recruited by Kentucky coach [[Tubby Smith]] and his replacement [[Billy Gillispie]].{{cite news |date=May 18, 2007 |title=Patterson's choice a surprise to the end |newspaper=The Herald-Dispatch |url=http://www.herald-dispatch.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20070518/SPORTS02/705180358/1014 |access-date=May 24, 2007}}{{dead link|date=September 2023}}{{cite web |year=2007 |title=Basketball Recruiting: Kentucky |url=http://kentucky.scout.com/a.z?s=48&p=9&c=8&cfg=bb&yr=2007 |url-status=dead |access-date=April 11, 2009 |work=Scout.com. |archive-date=October 5, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005051614/http://kentucky.scout.com/a.z?s=48&p=9&c=8&cfg=bb&yr=2007 }} Later, in the [[2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2009–10 season]], he played for former [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] coach [[John Calipari]] who became Gillispie's replacement in April 2009. ===Freshman season=== During Patterson's [[freshman]] All-American [[2007–08 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2007–08 season]], he averaged 16.4 [[point (basketball)|point]]s, 7.7 [[rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s, 1.2 [[block (basketball)|block]]s and 0.8 [[steal (basketball)|steal]]s, while shooting 57% from the [[field goal (basketball)|field]]. After a Kentucky victory over the [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss Rebels]], Patterson missed the remainder of the 2007–08 season with a [[stress fracture]] in his left ankle. He also claimed he planned on staying at Kentucky rather than participating in the [[NBA draft]]. ===Sophomore season=== [[File:Patrick Patterson vs. Florida.jpg|thumb|left|Patterson in 2009]] For his [[sophomore]] season at [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|UK]] during the [[2008–09 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2008–09 season]], he and teammate [[Jodie Meeks]] became one of the most successful duos that season, and also became the most productive duo at Kentucky, since the days of [[Dan Issel]] and [[Mike Pratt (basketball)|Mike Pratt]]. Patterson scored a career-high 33 points, on 15-of-17 shooting, on December 22, 2008, against the [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State Tigers]].{{Cite web |last=Associated Press |date=December 23, 2008 |title=Kentucky 102, Tennessee St. 58 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/283570096 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605170428/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/283570096 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 5, 2023 |access-date=June 5, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |quote=Patterson scored a career-high 33 points […] Patterson made 15 of 17 field goals}} During Patterson's sophomore 2008–09 season, he averaged 17.9 points, 9.3 rebounds, 2.1 blocks and 0.6 steals, while shooting 60% from the field. On April 18, 2009, Patterson decided to enter his name into the [[2009 NBA draft]]. However, on May 8, 2009, he decided he would return to Kentucky for the third season. ===Junior season=== Patterson continued to play a crucial role for the team during his junior season. However, with the addition of freshman players [[John Wall]], [[DeMarcus Cousins]] and [[Eric Bledsoe]], Patterson was no longer required to be the main option for scoring and rebounding. Patterson also improved his outside shot, shooting about 35% from the [[three-point line]] all season (compared to no three-pointers made in the previous seasons). During this season, Patterson helped the team win the [[2010 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] and achieve a #1 seed in the NCAA tournament for the first time since 2004. On April 23, 2010, Patterson entered the [[2010 NBA draft]]; by the time of the draft, he had completed his coursework and earned a degree from UK.{{cite web |last=Simmons |first=Bill |authorlink=Bill Simmons |date=June 25, 2010 |title=Bill Simmons: 2010 NBA draft diary - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/page2/story?page=simmons/100625 |access-date=June 5, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} ==Professional career== ===Houston Rockets (2010–2013)=== [[File:Patrick Patterson 2012.jpg|thumb|right|Patterson with the Houston Rockets in 2012]] On June 24, 2010, Patterson was selected in the NBA draft by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the fourteenth overall pick. On November 10, he was assigned to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web |title = Interview With The Agent: Odell McCants |publisher = SportsAgentBlog.com |date = June 21, 2010 |url = http://www.sportsagentblog.com/2010/06/21/interview-with-the-agent-odell-mccants/ |access-date = July 9, 2010 }} In nine games with the Vipers, Patterson averaged 18.3 points, and 10.3 rebounds in 35 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Patrick Patterson D-League statistics|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/nbdl/players/p/pattepa01d.html|publisher=basketball-reference|access-date=June 11, 2012}} Two days after being recalled by the Rockets,{{cite web |date=December 13, 2010 |title=Rockets recall Patterson |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/patterson121310.html |url-status=dead |access-date=June 11, 2012 |publisher=Rio Grande Valley Vipers |archive-date=November 19, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119055357/http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/patterson121310.html }} he made his NBA regular season debut on December 15, 2010.{{Cite web |title=Durant scores 32 as Thunder top Houston 117-105 |url=http://www.hcnonline.com/courier/sports/article_f585a895-972b-5d9e-ad29-2e131dad9ed1.html |url-status=dead |access-date=December 16, 2010 |archive-date=September 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190913072248/https://www.yourconroenews.com/sports/article/Durant-scores-32-as-Thunder-top-Houston-117-105-9278246.php }} With [[Luis Scola]] injured, Patterson had his first NBA start with the Rockets on March 14, 2011, scoring 2 points and grabbing 5 rebounds.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120714001743/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/boxscore;_ylt=AtymDh4jjeurpl7xsaTcMCOQvLYF?gid=2011031410|title=Yahoo! Sports box score}} After the Rockets used the [[amnesty clause]] to waive Scola, Patterson became the starting power forward for the [[2012–13 Houston Rockets season|2012–13 season]]. ===Sacramento
